name: eip-bandwidth-adjust
question: Does an elastic IP in ${region} with a bandwidth of ${start_mbit} Mbit/s read ${target_mbit} Mbit/s after the bandwidth is raised with PUT /v1/{project_id}/bandwidths/ID?
about: An EIP with its own bandwidth of 5 Mbit/s billed by traffic. The bandwidth id is read from the EIP, the size is read back (the control), the bandwidth is raised to 10 Mbit/s and read back once more. The EIP is released with its bandwidth and proven gone.

start_mbit.help: the bandwidth the EIP is made with, at most 5 Mbit/s

target_mbit.help: the bandwidth it is raised to, at most 10 Mbit/s

steps.says: an EIP with a dedicated bandwidth
steps.name: ${name}
steps.confirm: POST /v1/{project_id}/publicips with type 5_bgp and a dedicated bandwidth billed by traffic, the tag call and the find by the bandwidth name, all as in smn-http-confirm

steps.says: read the EIP and keep the id of its bandwidth
read the bandwidth before the change

steps.confirm: to confirm live: PUT /v1/{project_id}/bandwidths/ID with {bandwidth: {size}} is not called by the repository yet (OTC Elastic IP API reference, Updating a Bandwidth)

checks.says: the bandwidth starts at the size asked for
the bandwidth reads the raised size

eip.confirm: DELETE /v1/{project_id}/publicips/ID releases the EIP with its dedicated bandwidth, as in smn-http-confirm

kb.statement: The bandwidth of an EIP with a dedicated bandwidth in ${region} is raised from ${start_mbit} to ${target_mbit} Mbit/s with PUT /v1/{project_id}/bandwidths/ID and reads the new size at once.
